title: The Users page and the user details drawer in the admin portal

prose.label: Users page.
prose.text: {{users-page}} {{users-columns}} The active-only listing and the State column are unreconciled {{gap:users-state-column}}. The page's filter wording is unclear {{gap:users-filter-wording}}.

prose.label: User details drawer.
prose.text: {{user-drawer-tabs}} {{user-drawer-findings}} {{user-drawer-alerts}} The verdict values differ from the Agentic SOC Alerts page {{divergence:alert-verdict-values}}. {{user-drawer-tenants-groups}} The Details tab lists two Name fields {{gap:details-name-fields}}.

users-page.statement: The Users page (Agentic SOC > Users, Identities > Users or AEM > Users) lists only active users, aggregated from different sources, and exports the list to CSV.

quotes: Only users in an active state are displayed on the Users page.
On the Users page (Agentic SOC > Users, Identities > Users, or AEM > Users)
Aggregate users from different sources for a centralized view.
Export the list of users and their associated details as a CSV file.

users-columns.statement: User list columns include Is Admin, Total Identity Findings (critical, high, medium and low), Sources (for example Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID), Identity Type (User, Service Principal or Special Identities), State (Active or Inactive) and Type (Internal or External).

quotes: Modify the columns displayed in the table.
View the list of users. Click a user to view detailed information. For each user, you can see:
Is Admin: The user's admin role status. If the user is an admin, this field shows true.
Total Identity Findings: The total number of critical, high, medium, and low identity findings for the user.
Sources: The source of the user (e.g., Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, etc.).
Identity Type: The type of identity (User, Service Principal, or Special Identities).
State: The state of the user's account (Active or Inactive).
Type: The type of user (Internal or External).

user-drawer-tabs.statement: The user details drawer has Details, Identity Findings, Alerts, Tenants and Groups tabs, and the Identity Findings, Alerts, Tenants and Groups tabs each have an Export as CSV icon.

quotes: In the user details drawer, you can access the following tabs:
On the Identity Findings tab, you can do the following:
On the Alerts tab, you can do the following:
On the Tenants tab, you can do the following:
On the Groups tab, you can do the following:
Click the Export as CSV icon to export the identity findings list for a user to a CSV file.
Click the Export as CSV icon to export the alerts list to a CSV file.
Click the Export as CSV icon to export the tenants list to a CSV file.
Click the Export as CSV icon to export the groups list to a CSV file.

user-drawer-findings.statement: In the Identity Findings tab, severity is Critical, High, Medium or Low with Critical and High listed first, and Type of Risk gives categories such as Kerberos Abuse, Account Management and Credential Exposure.

quotes: Identity Finding Severity: The severity level (Critical, High, Medium, or Low). The Critical and High severity findings are listed first.
Type of Risk: The type of risk (e.g., Kerberos Abuse, Account Management, Credential Exposure, etc.).

user-drawer-alerts.statement: In the Alerts tab, the severity score ranges from 0 to 10 (higher is more critical), and the Alert Verdict takes values such as Accepted, Executed, Partial, Proposed, Scheduled, Success, under Review or Recommendation Status Unspecified.

quotes: The severity score ranges from 0 to 10, with higher scores indicating greater criticality and requiring immediate remediation.
Alert Verdict: The verdict for the alert (Accepted, Executed, Partial, Proposed, Scheduled, Success, under Review, or Recommendation Status Unspecified).

user-drawer-tenants-groups.statement: The Tenants tab shows Tenant Severity (Critical, High, Medium or Low), total identity findings and total alerts; the Groups tab shows the Group Key (a unique identifier for the group associated with a user) and when the group was last updated.

quotes: Tenant Severity: The severity score reflects the seriousness of identity findings for each tenant (e.g., Critical, High, Medium, or Low).
Total Alerts: The total number of alerts created for a user.
Group Key: A unique identifier used to identify the group associated with a user.
Group Last Updated: The date when the group was last updated.
Total Identity Findings: The total number of identity findings for a user.

users-state-column.title: Why a State column (Active or Inactive) exists if only active users are listed
users-state-column.detail: The About Users page says only users in an active state are displayed, yet its column list describes State as 'Active or Inactive'. No captured text says whether inactive users can appear, for example through a filter or saved view.

users-filter-wording.title: What the Users page filter line covers
users-filter-wording.detail: The Users page filter line reads 'Filter assets by Name, Type, Identity Type, or Sources.' (it says assets); no captured text states the filters available for users.

details-name-fields.title: What the two Name fields on the user details drawer's Details tab hold
details-name-fields.detail: The Viewing User Details page lists both 'Name: The name of the user.' and 'Name: The first name of the user.' on the Details tab, with no last-name field; which is correct is not stated.

alert-verdict-values.summary: The user details drawer lists Alert Verdict values Accepted, Executed, Partial, Proposed, Scheduled, Success, under Review and Recommendation Status Unspecified, while the Agentic SOC Alerts page gives Malicious, Suspicious and Benign as example verdicts; the drawer opens from Agentic SOC > Users as well.

positions.says: Alert Verdict takes recommendation-status values such as Accepted, Executed and Success.

quotes: Alert Verdict: The verdict for the alert (Accepted, Executed, Partial, Proposed, Scheduled, Success, under Review, or Recommendation Status Unspecified).

positions.says: An alert's verdict is, for example, Malicious, Suspicious or Benign.

quotes: Verdict: The verdict for the alert (e.g., Malicious, Suspicious, Benign)

alert-verdict-values.impact: Which verdict values an analyst sees in the user drawer's Alerts tab, versus the Alerts page, is unclear; the Accepted/Executed list may be a copy of recommendation statuses.
